# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [today's date]

**To:** UPMC Health Plan — Appeals Department
[appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:** Riley Jennings
[my mailing address]
[my phone number]

**RE: Appeal of prior authorization denial dated 2026-08-19**
- **Member:** Riley Jennings
- **Member ID:** W995720068
- **Reference number:** POC-39DE00339B-16726
- **Service denied:** Knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery, CPT 29881
- **Plan:** UPMC Health Plan (Commercial/ACA), Pennsylvania

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing UPMC Health Plan's decision of 2026-08-19 denying prior authorization for knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery (CPT 29881), reference number POC-39DE00339B-16726. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and approve the surgery my surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that I need.

The notice states that the request was denied because the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. The notice also states that the determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria. I want to address the documentation point directly, because the prior authorization packet contains a detailed and dated clinical record, which I have set out below.

## An important note on the plan's criteria

I want to be straightforward about one thing in this letter: **I have not been given the text of the criteria the plan applied, so I am not quoting the plan anywhere in this appeal.** The denial notice refers to the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria, but it does not include them, and no criteria document was provided to me. I am therefore not in a position to state what threshold, duration, or finding the plan requires — and I am not going to guess at one. Everything below is a statement of what is in my own records.

## Request for the criteria relied upon (please respond to this in writing)

I understand that UPMC Health Plan uses InterQual, which is licensed software rather than a publicly posted document. I am nonetheless requesting, in writing and free of charge, **the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination**, along with any internal rule, guideline, or protocol relied upon in denying CPT 29881 for me. Federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules require the plan to provide the specific rule or criterion relied on for an adverse benefit determination at no cost to the member. The plan holds these criteria; I do not. Without them, I cannot know which specific element the plan considered missing, and I ask that the plan either provide them or identify precisely what document or finding it believes is absent so it can be supplied.

## What my records actually contain

Here is what was documented in the prior authorization packet, as the records state it:

**Symptoms and duration.** Nine months of progressive pain in the knee, unrelieved by rest.

**Supervised conservative care.** Supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion: 10 weeks, from 2026-05-08 to 2026-07-17, with 16 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

**Medication and injection.** NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief. A corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-13 gave 2 weeks of partial relief.

**Imaging.** MRI of the knee on 2026-07-18: displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking; articular cartilage preserved, Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1.

**Physical examination.** Positive provocative testing on the affected side; range of motion limited by pain.

**Function.** I have locking and giving way in the knee. I cannot squat or kneel. I am limited to level walking.

**Surgical safety factors.** No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

**Treating surgeon.** Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed.

## Why I am asking the plan to look again

The denial rests on incomplete documentation. The record above is dated, specific, and attributable: a nine-month symptom history, a completed and discharge-documented course of supervised physical therapy with the dates and visit count recorded, a documented medication trial and a dated injection with the duration of relief noted, an MRI with a specific structural diagnosis, examination findings, and a functional description. My surgeon's documentation of medical necessity is part of that packet.

If some particular item is still considered missing, I am asking the plan to name it. A denial for incomplete documentation that does not identify the specific missing element leaves me and my surgeon with no way to cure the defect. Identifying it — and providing the criteria against which my file was measured — is within the plan's control, and I am asking the plan to do both.

## Closing request

I respectfully request that UPMC Health Plan:

1. Overturn the denial dated 2026-08-19 (reference POC-39DE00339B-16726) and authorize knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery, CPT 29881;
2. Provide me, in writing and free of charge, the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination, plus any other internal rule or guideline relied upon; and
3. If the denial is maintained, state specifically which documentation element was considered missing and identify the reviewer's credentials, so that my surgeon can respond directly.

I understand my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-02-15**. I am submitting this appeal to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I understand I may also file through the member secure website (including by email or live chat) or by phone at 1-888-876-2756 (group) or 1-866-353-3598 (individual), TTY 711.

I am also enclosing supporting records and authorizing my treating surgeon and their office to speak with the plan and submit additional information on my behalf.

Thank you for reconsidering this decision. I would appreciate written confirmation that this appeal has been received.

Sincerely,

---

**Riley Jennings**
Member ID: W995720068
[my mailing address]
[my phone number]
[my email address]
Date: [today's date]

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of the denial notice dated 2026-08-19 (reference POC-39DE00339B-16726)
- Physical therapy discharge note, 2026-05-08 to 2026-07-17 (16 visits)
- MRI report of the knee, 2026-07-18
- Office notes and letter of medical necessity from Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery
- [any additional records my surgeon's office is submitting]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
